title: Global EV sales reach 2.15 million units in September 2026
gist: Benchmark reports 2.15M EVs sold globally in September 2026 (+17% MoM, -2% YoY; 15.5M YTD, +3%). Record Europe (+39% YoY) offset a 44% North America drop against a pre-tax-credit-expiry comparison and a weak China (-18%), where record NEV exports of 558,000 and a new EU hybrid cap and VAT rebate cut shape 2027 export risk.

insights.claim: Global EV sales were 2.15 million units in September 2026, up 17% month-on-month but down 2% year-on-year, bringing 2026 year-to-date sales to 15.5 million, up 3% on the same period last year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Global volume growth is only low single digits, so battery-materials demand now hinges on regional mix.
insights.quote: Global EV sales rebounded in September, rising 17% month-on-month to 2.15 million units

insights.claim: Europe sold almost 600,000 EVs in September 2026, a monthly record 10% above the June 2026 high, with sales up 39% year-on-year and 62% month-on-month, lifting year-to-date growth to 30%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Europe is the main source of incremental global EV demand in 2026.
insights.quote: Europe had its strongest month on record

insights.claim: European growth is led by battery electric vehicles (+50% YoY) rather than plug-in hybrids (+16% YoY), and the UK, France, Spain, Portugal and Finland all set record monthly EV sales.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The BEV-heavy mix favours full-battery chemistries and nickel/lithium demand over PHEV-weighted growth.

insights.claim: France's EV sales rose 78% year-on-year to almost 80,000 units and Germany's rose 61% to 117,000 in September 2026, while UK penetration was flat near 40% and its 3.5x monthly jump reflects the September plate change.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Underlying UK demand did not accelerate; France and Germany are the real growth engines.
insights.quote: UK EV sales grew more than 3.5 times month-on-month

insights.claim: The EU and China agreed to cap Chinese-built full and plug-in hybrid imports at 350,000 units a year from 2027 for four years, rising 6% annually from the second year, pending EU member state approval.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Caps a channel Chinese OEMs were using to bypass BEV tariffs; watch member-state approval.
insights.quote: imports of Chinese-made full and plug-in hybrids will be capped at 350,000 units a year from 2027

insights.claim: The European Commission expects the cap to more than halve Chinese hybrid shipments versus the up to 800,000 units China could export to the EU in 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Implies sizeable redirected Chinese export volume or lower shipments from 2027.

insights.claim: China-made vehicles made up 29% of PHEVs sold across the EU, EFTA and UK year-to-date in 2026, more than double the 14% share in 2025, which is why the cap targets this segment.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Rapid share gain explains the political urgency; European PHEV makers may benefit.
insights.quote: around 14% of PHEVs sold across the EU, EFTA and UK in 2025 were made in China

insights.claim: North American EV sales fell 44% year-on-year in September 2026, the steepest decline of the year, leaving the region down 24% year-to-date, because the base month was September 2025 when buyers rushed ahead of the US federal EV tax credit expiry.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The decline is a comparison effect, not a fresh demand deterioration; do not extrapolate it.
insights.quote: rather than a fresh deterioration in demand

insights.claim: From October 2026 year-on-year comparisons will be against the first months without the US tax credit, when EV sales collapsed, so North American YoY declines should narrow significantly.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Expect optically improving North American YoY EV data from Q4 2026 without real demand recovery.
insights.quote: the year-on-year picture should improve markedly

insights.claim: China's EV sales fell 18% year-on-year in September 2026, widening from -11% in August, leaving the market down 13% year-to-date, with plug-in hybrids down 25% and BEVs down 6%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Domestic weakness is concentrated in PHEVs; BEV demand is more resilient.
insights.quote: China’s year-on-year decline widened to 18% in September

insights.claim: Chinese manufacturers are holding production steady and shipping the surplus abroad, pushing passenger car NEV exports to a record 558,000 units in September 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Domestic oversupply is being exported, pressuring pricing in overseas markets.
insights.quote: Manufacturers have continued to hold production steady and send the surplus overseas

insights.claim: China will cut its NEV export VAT rebate from 13% to 9% from 1 April 2027, which together with the EU hybrid cap could weigh on Chinese export volumes and overseas profitability next year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Two 2027 headwinds for Chinese export growth; watch for pull-forward exports in late 2026 and Q1 2027.
insights.quote: raising the cost of exporting and putting further pressure on automakers’ overseas profitability

insights.claim: EV penetration of China's passenger car market remains strong because weakness in the wider auto market is weighing on ICE sales at least as heavily as on EVs.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Falling EV volumes in China do not signal share loss to ICE.
insights.quote: weakness in the wider auto market is weighing on ICE sales at least as heavily
